items.stem:
Read the following extract on appointment, transfer and removal of judges and answer the questions that follow.
"Security of tenure, fixed salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund and restrictions on discussing judges' conduct protect judicial independence. The removal of a judge requires a motion passed in each House by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting. A distinguished jurist in the President's opinion can be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court."
(i) A judge of the Supreme Court retires at the age of: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'collegium system' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Salaries of judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. (2)
items.answer: (i) 65 years (ii) The system in which the Chief Justice of India and senior-most judges of the Supreme Court recommend appointments and transfers of judges. (iii) They are not subject to a vote of Parliament, which protects judicial independence.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Habeas corpus can be issued against both public authorities and private persons. Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or the Governors. The writ jurisdiction of High Courts under Article 226 is wider, as it extends to fundamental rights and 'any other purpose'. Prohibition is issued while proceedings are pending; certiorari is issued after the order is passed."
(i) Explain the term 'prohibition', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Habeas corpus protects personal liberty. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Article 226 is narrower than Article 32." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) A writ issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop it from acting beyond its jurisdiction while the case is pending. (ii) It requires the detaining authority to produce the person and justify the detention. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Article 226 is wider, as High Courts can issue writs for any other purpose as well.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) A writ issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop it from acting beyond its jurisdiction while the case is pending. (ii) It requires the detaining authority to produce the person and justify the detention.
